title: When its Conforming to be Unique
summary: Kahran and Divya tug at the contradiction inside trying to be unique — how queer and artist circles celebrate weirdness while New England wealth, East Asian cultures and Rajasthani families ratchet you toward conformity. They argue the floor and ceiling of acceptable behaviour is set culturally, and that nonconformity on one axis (religion, sexuality, art) tends to cascade into others.
topics: succeeding before being allowed to be different

intents.display: to think about whether being unique is its own kind of conformity
